topic: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards

audits.title: Audit on resuscitation equipment in Carseview Centre (NHS Tayside)
audits.standard: Local NHS Tayside Emergency Equipment Protocol
audits.setting: Carseview Centre (3 adult wards, IPCU and learning disability unit), NHS Tayside

cycle1.result: Trolleys lacked ligature packs, masks not by oxygen cylinders, dextro-tablets not readily available; learning disability unit had no resuscitation trolley.

audits.intervention: Feedback to wards, multidisciplinary meetings and an updated local protocol (finalised November 2020) with recommendations.

cycle2.result: Trolleys better equipped in line with the updated protocol; missing items varied by ward but none consistent across the site; all recommendations implemented.

audits.other_findings: Additional items such as nebuliser and non-rebreather masks were stocked but hard to locate.
audits.citation: Leung T, Zariddin L, Megoran E. Audit on resuscitation equipment in Carseview Centre (NHS Tayside). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S36-S36. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.148.

audits.title: A closed loop two cycle audit investigating the availability and accessibility of physical healthcare equipment on forensic inpatient wards within mersey care's secure division
audits.standard: CQC 2019 'Brief Guide: Physical Healthcare in Mental Health Settings' recommended equipment
audits.setting: Forensic inpatient wards (low, medium, high and secure LD), Mersey Care secure division

cycle1.result: Mean equipment availability 66% (range 50.9%–88.9%) in secure wards versus 75% (61.1%–88.9%) in non-secure control wards.

audits.intervention: Findings presented and physical health equipment boxes placed in ward clinic rooms.
audits.other_findings: Gloves, pulse oximeters, sphygmomanometers, thermometers and stethoscopes became available on all wards, but secure wards still lagged the non-secure controls; further re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Davies T, Owens S, Forjoe T. A closed loop two cycle audit investigating the availability and accessibility of physical healthcare equipment on forensic inpatient wards within mersey care's secure division. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S74-S74. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.236.

audits.title: Availability and Functionality of Physical Health and Resuscitation Equipment in an Inpatient Setting: A Closed Loop Audit Cycle
audits.standard: RCPsych Physical Health in Mental Health scoping group report and Resuscitation Council UK Mental Health Inpatient Care Equipment and Drug Lists
audits.setting: Four acute adult inpatient wards, mental health hospital, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Overall 90.0% of standards met; physical health equipment 83.8%; resuscitation equipment 94.2%.

audits.intervention: Awareness presentations at governance meetings, complete equipment sets on each ward, registration of equipment on maintenance database with engineering servicing, weekly (previously monthly) resuscitation checks

cycle2.result: Overall 90.0% (144/160 items available and functional); physical health equipment 76.6% (49/64); resuscitation equipment 99.2% (95/96).

audits.other_findings: Physical health equipment availability fell. Proposed named staff checker, physical health equipment checklist and electronic 'My Kit Check' platform.
audits.citation: Tang S, Fadlalla I. Availability and Functionality of Physical Health and Resuscitation Equipment in an Inpatient Setting: A Closed Loop Audit Cycle. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S178-S179. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.496.

audits.title: Audit of Resuscitation Equipment in a Mental Health Setting – Resulting in Trust-Wide Action
audits.standard: Local Trust policy and Resuscitation Council UK standards for resuscitation equipment and weekly checklists

cycle1.result: 7/10 locations did not meet standards (missing or expired adrenaline, suction, oxygen masks); 4/10 wards had not completed the weekly checklist; 70% of staff-completed checklists were incorrect.

audits.intervention: Updated, more detailed checklist, standardised procedure for ward managers, regular audits and extra Resuscitation team staffing.
audits.other_findings: A re-audit was done and changes are being rolled out Trust-wide, but re-audit results are not reported.
audits.citation: Knowles N, Husain N. Audit of Resuscitation Equipment in a Mental Health Setting – Resulting in Trust-Wide Action. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S243-S243. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.591.

audits.title: Closing the Gap: Ensuring Minimum Required Physical Health Equipment Is Available on Inpatient Wards: An Audit
audits.standard: RCPsych Physical Health in Mental Health (2009) equipment checklist; compliance standard 100%
audits.setting: Seven inpatient wards (acute adult, older adult, forensic), The Redwoods Centre, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: All wards >80% compliant; overall compliance 87%; neurological testing pins absent on most wards; alcometers, Snellen charts, ophthalmoscopes and otoscopes borrowed between wards.

audits.intervention: Formal equipment-sharing arrangements confirmed and procurement of missing equipment planned
audits.other_findings: Re-audit planned 6 months after the first cycle.
audits.citation: Obaid H, Capraro M, Evans H, Maumi G. Closing the Gap: Ensuring Minimum Required Physical Health Equipment Is Available on Inpatient Wards: An Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S327-S327. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11805.
